Hi folks,

Very recently I have merged a PR (lean4#14357) that implements stateful linters. Each linter has a global state. User has to specify the initial state and at then end of elaborating each command, the linter has to provide a new value. If the linter crashes, we just hot-circuit and pass the old value of the state.

To accommodate cross-linter communication (for example, when we want to have one producer linter that computes something and several consumer linters that read that value) in a simplest possible way, we split such linters into two phases: early and late.

The main high-level principles are the following:

  • In early phase, we read linter's previous state and produce an intermediate value passed to the late phase. This intermediate value is wrapped in an Option type; if the early phase fails, none is passed to the late phase.
  • In late phase, we read linter's previous state and the early phase's intermediate state to produce and save a new state. If this phase fails, the state remains unchanged.

When it comes to data sharing, we can do the following:

  • In both phases, we can read previous value of any linter.
  • In late phase, we can read both previous value of any linter, as well as intermediate state from early phase of any linter.

Here is a simple example:

import Lean

open Lean Elab Command

/-- Persistent (`σ`) state of `emitter`: the running command count. -/
structure Counter where
  count : Nat

/-- Pre-phase handoff (`τ`) of `emitter`: the count computed for the current command. -/
structure Payload where
  current : Nat

initialize emitter : StatefulLinter Counter Payload ←
  registerStatefulLinter (Counter.mk 0)
    (pre := fun stx self _ =>
      pure <| if Parser.isTerminalCommand stx then none else some { current := self.count + 1 })
    (post := fun _ self preState _ _ =>
      pure { count := (preState.map Payload.current).getD self.count })

def registerReader (emitter : StatefulLinter Counter Payload) (label : String) :
    IO Unit := do
  let _ ← registerStatefulLinter (τ := Unit) (Counter.mk 0)
    (post := fun _ self _ _ readPre => do
      if let some p := readPre emitter then
        logInfo m!"{label} sees count {p.current}"
      pure self)

initialize
  registerReader emitter "reader A"
  registerReader emitter "reader B"
  registerReader emitter "reader C"

emitter is a linter that persists number of seen commands (stored in Counter type). The intermediate state (that can be read by other linters) is given by Payload type. If we are not in terminal command, we increment the global value in the early phase, and in the late phase we store it.

registerReader takes a typed handle to the emitting linter, and in the late phase just reads the intermediate (Payload) value. We can register multiple such linters, and each of them will read the value produced by emitter.

In stateful linters, when we read our own previous/intermediate state, we have an immediate access to it in the signature of the early/late phase (the self arguments in the example). When reading information from other linter, we need a typed handle and we are given a closure that given a handle, returns a value (i.e. accessing the intermediate value of the emitter in the example).
When I saw this commit I thought maybe linter.style.header in Mathlib could be refactored to use this feature. When designing this, were there some particular linters you had in mind?
Hmm, this particular linter sounds like a good suggestion. I was original thinking of even simpler things, like permitting only a certain number of declarations in file and linting that.

Cool! This is useful for a superfluousExpose that I have as a draft in #39387. Without this it was necessary to fire at the end of file and do awkward text scanning for the @[expose] public section, with this the linter can scope state across commands, fire once per sectior, anchor the warning at the header properly...

Refactoring minImports (#42186, to avoid an IORef in favor of the linter state -- this also recovers parallel elaboration) surfaced lean4#14581, what do you think @Wojciech Różowski ?
lean4#14581 looks good to me. I will merge it, once it passes the mathlib ci
#42186 makes the minImports linter stateful; #42201 makes the header linter stateful (stacked on top so that minImports can consume the header linter)
